questions.question: In a circular race of 950 m length, A and B start with speeds of 18 km/h and 36 km/h, respectively, in the same direction, at the same time, from the same point. After how many seconds will they meet for the first time at the starting point?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of the circular track (L) = 950 m

Speed of A (SA) = 18 km/h = 18 × (1000/3600) m/s = 5 m/s

Speed of B (SB) = 36 km/h = 36 × (1000/3600) m/s = 10 m/s

**Formula used:**

Time to meet at the starting point = Length of track / Relative speed

**Calculation:**

Relative speed (Sᵣₑₗ) = Speed of B - Speed of A = 10 m/s - 5 m/s = 5 m/s

⇒ Time to meet at the starting point = 950 m / 5 m/s

⇒ Time = 190 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: Two runners, Sony and Mony, start running on a circular track of length 200 m at speeds of 18 and 24 km/h, respectively, in the same direction. After how much time from the start will they meet again at the starting point?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sony and Mony, start running on a circular track of length 200 m at speeds of 18 and 24 km/h, respectively, in the same direction.

Formula used:

When two runners run on a circular track of length D m at a m/sec and b m/sec, respectively, in the same direction.

Time taken by them to meet for the first time at starting point on the track

⇒ LCM (D/a , D/b)

**Calculation:**

The speed of Sony (S₁) = 18 km/hr

⇒ 18 x (5/18) = 5 m/sec

The speed of Mony (S₂) = 24 km/hr

⇒ 24 x (5/18) = 20/3 m/sec

Time taken by them to meet for the first time at the starting point on track

⇒ LCM (D/a , D/b)

⇒ LCM (200/5, 200/(20/3))

⇒ LCM (40, 30)

 40 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 5

 30 = 2 x 3 x 5

⇒ LCM (40, 30) = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 5 = 120 seconds

**∴ The required time is 120 seconds.**

questions.question: Ruksana travelled at 60 km/h while going from point A to point B and returned via the same route at a different speed. If Ruksana’s overall average speed during the two-way journey was 48 km/h, what was her speed while travelling from B to A?
questions.solution:

The speed of the car is travelling is 60 km/hr and Average Speed is 48 km/hr

Average speed = Total distance/Total time

Time = Distance/Speed

2x/48 = x/60 + x/S

⇒ 2x/48 - x/60 = x/S

⇒3x/120 = x/S

Required speed = S = 40 km/hr

questions.question: A thief, seeing a policeman from a distance of 120 metres, starts running at a speed of 7 km/h. The policeman chases immediately with a speed of 8 km/h and the thief is caught. What is the distance run by the thief?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance between policemen and thief = 120 m

Speed of the thief = 7 km/h

Speed of policeman = 8 km/h

**Concept Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Relative speed = 8 – 7 = 1 km/h [they are running in the same direction]

⇒ 1 km/h = 1 × (5)/(18) = (5)/(18) m/s

⇒ Time taken to cover 120 m = (120)/(frac{5){18}} = (120 ×18)/(5) = 432 s

⇒ Speed of the thief = 7 km/h = 7 × (5)/(18) = (35)/(18) m/s

⇒ Distance covered by the thief in 432 s = (35)/(18) × 432 = 840 m

**Therefore, thief runs 840 m before he is caught by the policemen**

questions.question: Varun and Sandeep started for a car race from the same point, in the same direction and at the same time on a circular track of length 1635 m with the speeds of 90 km/h and 108 km/h, respectively. After how much time (in s) will they meet again for the first time?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (same direction) = 108 − 90 = 18 km/h

Relative speed in m/s = 18 × (5/18) = 5 m/s

Time to meet = Distance ÷ Relative speed

Time to meet = 1635 ÷ 5 = 327 s

**∴ The correct answer is 327 s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the circular track = 1635 m

Speed of Varun = 90 km/h

Speed of Sandeep = 108 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c9ae52f2f06fd1987c4e94a36dbf802929c1466ca3c897098f772c34b395131f.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time to meet for the first time = Track Length ÷ Relative Speed

Relative speed (same direction) = S₁ − S₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of Varun = 90 × (5/18) = 25 m/s

⇒ Speed of Sandeep = 108 × (5/18) = 30 m/s

⇒ Relative speed = 30 − 25 = 5 m/s

⇒ Time to meet = 1635 ÷ 5 = 327 s

**∴ The correct answer is 327 s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting for the first time anywhere on the track

When moving in the same direction: Time = Distance ÷ (S₁ − S₂). When moving in opposite directions: Time = Distance ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Meeting at the starting point

The time taken to meet at the starting point for the first time is the LCM of the times taken by each individual to complete one full round.

Relative Speed

Relative speed is the speed of a moving object with respect to another. If they move in the same direction, speeds subtract; if opposite, speeds add.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.
</p

questions.question: In a circular race of 840 m, A and B start running in the same direction at the same time from the same point at the speeds of 6 m/s and 12 m/s, respectively. After how much time will they meet next?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two persons run in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their speeds.

Relative speed = 12 − 6 = 6 m/s.

Time to meet next = Track length ÷ Relative speed.

Time = 840 ÷ 6 = 140 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 140 s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b79b7c70c3142a9947d29865cd34de0c1710c29b6dd3c67e79a8672f9be1b85c.png] 

**Given:**

⇒ Total length of the circular track = 840 m

⇒ Speed of runner A = 6 m/s

⇒ Speed of runner B = 12 m/s

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Time taken to meet = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Since both A and B are running in the same direction, their relative speed will be the difference between their speeds.

⇒ Relative Speed = Speed of B − Speed of A

⇒ Relative Speed = 12 − 6 = 6 m/s

⇒ Time taken to meet next = 840 ÷ 6

⇒ Time = 140 s

**∴ The correct answer is 140 s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting Anywhere on Track (First Time)

Time = Track Length ÷ Relative Speed. If moving in the same direction, RS = |S₁ − S₂|. If opposite, RS = S₁ + S₂.

Meeting at the Starting Point (First Time)

Time = LCM of the individual times taken to complete one full round = LCM(L÷S₁, L÷S₂).

Number of Distinct Meeting Points

If the ratio of their speeds is a : b (in simplest form), they meet at |a − b| distinct points if moving in the same direction, and (a + b) points if moving in opposite directions.
</p

questions.question: In a circular race of 750 m, X and Y start from the same point and at the same time with speeds of 9 km/h and 13.5 km/h, respectively. If they are running in the same direction then, when will they meet again for the first time on the track?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When running in the same direction, relative speed is the difference between the two speeds.

Relative Speed = 13.5 − 9 = 4.5 km/h

Convert to m/s: 4.5 × (5/18) = 1.25 m/s

Time to meet = Track Length ÷ Relative Speed = 750 ÷ 1.25 = 600 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 600 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance of the circular track = 750 m

Speed of runner X = 9 km/h

Speed of runner Y = 13.5 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time to meet for the first time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Speed in m/s = Speed in km/h × (5/18)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/12a58afd3c329149524568441fe25e59774cb4a9f72d374f61d5c5f1d8ff93cf.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of X in m/s = 9 × (5/18) = 2.5 m/s

⇒ Speed of Y in m/s = 13.5 × (5/18) = 3.75 m/s

⇒ Relative speed (same direction) = Speed of Y − Speed of X

⇒ Relative speed = 3.75 − 2.5 = 1.25 m/s

⇒ Time to meet = 750 ÷ 1.25

⇒ Time to meet = 75000 ÷ 125 = 600 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 600 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting Anywhere on the Track (Same Direction)

Time to meet for the first time anywhere on the track = Track Length ÷ (S₁ − S₂).

Meeting Anywhere on the Track (Opposite Direction)

Time to meet for the first time anywhere on the track = Track Length ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Meeting at the Starting Point

To find when runners will meet exactly at the starting point, calculate the time taken by each to complete one round, then take their LCM: LCM(T₁, T₂).

Number of Distinct Meeting Points

If the ratio of speeds is a:b (in lowest terms), the number of distinct meeting points is |a − b| for same direction, and a + b for opposite direction.
</p

questions.question: A policeman received information that a thief is at a distance of 1.5 km from him. The thief starts moving by car and the policeman chases him by car. The thief and the policeman are moving at the speeds of 90 km/h and 120 km/h respectively. At what distance (in km) will the police catch the thief?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance between policeman and thief = 1.5 km

Speed of the thief = 90 km/h

Speed of the policeman = 120 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed = Speed of policeman - Speed of thief

Distance = Relative speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Relative speed = 120 km/h - 90 km/h

Relative speed = 30 km/h

Let the time taken to catch the thief be t hours.

Distance covered by the policeman in time t = Distance covered by the thief in time t + Initial distance

120t = 90t + 1.5

⇒ 120t - 90t = 1.5

⇒ 30t = 1.5

⇒ t = 1.5 / 30

⇒ t = 0.05 hours

Distance at which the policeman catches the thief = Speed of policeman × Time

Distance = 120 km/h × 0.05 hours

Distance = 6 km

**The police will catch the thief at a distance of 6 km.**

When crossed each other (moving in opp. direction)

questions.question: A thief running at 7 km/h is chased by a policeman whose speed is 12 km/h. If the thief is 280 m ahead of the policeman, then the time required for the policeman to catch the thief will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the thief = 7 km/h

Speed of the policeman = 12 km/h

Distance between the thief and the policeman = 280 m

**Concept:**

Relative speed is the difference in speeds when two objects move in the same direction.

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance / Relative Speed

**Calculation:**

Convert distance into km:

⇒ 280 m = 280/1000 km = 0.28 km

Calculate relative speed:

⇒ Relative Speed = 12 km/h - 7 km/h = 5 km/h

Calculate time required to catch the thief:

⇒ Time = Distance / Relative Speed

⇒ Time = 0.28 km / 5 km/h

⇒ Time = 0.056 hours

Convert time into minutes:

⇒ Time = 0.056 × 60 minutes

⇒ Time = 3.36 minutes

Convert decimal minutes into fraction:

⇒ Time = 3 (9/25) minutes

**∴ The time required for the policeman to catch the thief is 3 (9/25) minutes.**

questions.question: A student takes 1.25 hours to travel from home to school at a speed of 4km/h. By what percentage should he increase his speed to reduce the time by 25% to cover the same distance from school to home?
questions.solution:

Distance between home and school = 4 × 1.25 = 5 km

New time = 1.25 × (3/4) = 15/16 hr

New speed = 5/(15/16) = (5 × 16)/15 = 16/3

For savings time take ratio

Ratio of original speed to new speed = 4 : 16/3 = 3 : 4

Let original speed = 3 and New speed = 4

Speed increased by = 4 - 3 = 1

∴ Speed increased by (in %) = 1/3 × 100 = 33(1)/(3)\% 

**Short Trick:**

Let time taking in the starting be 4 unit

New time = 4 × 3/4 = 3 unit

Ratio of original to new = 4 : 3

As we know,

Speed is inversely proportional to time, then

Speed ratio original to new = 3 : 4

∴ Required speed = 1/3 × 100 = 33(1)/(3)\%

questions.question: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 200 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The thief and the policeman run at the rate of 10 km/h and 11 km/h, respectively. What is the distance (in metres) between them after 9 minutes?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed = 11 − 10 = 1 km/h = 1000 ÷ 60 m/min = 50/3 m/min.

Remaining distance = Initial distance − Distance covered = 200 − 150 = 50 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 50 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Initial distance between policeman and thief = 200 m

Speed of policeman = 11 km/h

Speed of thief = 10 km/h

Time = 9 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (when moving in the same direction) = S₁ − S₂

Distance = Speed × Time

1 km/h = 5/18 m/s

⇒ Relative speed = 11 − 10 = 1 km/h

⇒ Relative speed in m/s = 1 × (5/18) = 5/18 m/s

⇒ Time in seconds = 9 × 60 = 540 seconds

⇒ Distance covered by policeman relative to thief = Relative speed × Time

⇒ Relative distance = (5/18) × 540 = 5 × 30 = 150 m

⇒ Remaining distance between them = Initial distance − Relative distance

⇒ Remaining distance = 200 − 150 = 50 m

**∴ The correct answer is 50 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗ = S₁ − S₂.

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗ = S₁ + S₂.

Speed Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the speed value by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: A man completes a journey in ten hours. He travels at a speed of 21 km/h for the first half of the journey and at a speed of 24 km/h for the second half. Calculate the total distance travelled (in kilometers).

⇒ Average speed = 1008 / 45 = 22.4 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 224 km.**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

When a person travels two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed is given by 2xy / (x + y).

Average Speed for Equal Time Intervals

When a person travels at speeds x and y for equal intervals of time, the average speed is the arithmetic mean, given by (x + y) / 2.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (x + y). If they move in the same direction, the relative speed is the difference of their speeds (x − y).

questions.question: Arvind and Chetan started running simultaneously from the same point in the same direction on a circular track of length 210 m. If Arvind takes 180 seconds to complete one round, and Chetan takes 420 seconds to complete one round, after how much time will they meet for the first time at the starting point on the track?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time taken by Arvind to complete one round = 180 seconds = 3 minutes.

Time taken by Chetan to complete one round = 420 seconds = 7 minutes.

To find the time they meet for the first time at the starting point, we calculate the LCM of their individual lap times.

Meeting time = LCM(3, 7) = 21 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 21 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of circular track = 210 m

Time taken by Arvind (T₁) = 180 seconds

Time taken by Chetan (T₂) = 420 seconds

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d3f3d0dadcdbfb6f2f5ebccd64d5bb528d1c478001af304c84d8ffdbcc9c5153.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time to meet for the first time at the starting point = LCM of individual times taken to complete one round.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 180 = 2² × 3² × 5

⇒ Prime factorization of 420 = 2² × 3 × 5 × 7

⇒ LCM(180, 420) = 2² × 3² × 5 × 7

⇒ LCM(180, 420) = 4 × 9 × 5 × 7 = 1260 seconds

⇒ Convert total seconds into minutes = 1260 ÷ 60

⇒ Time to meet = 21 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 21 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting First Time at Starting Point

When multiple people start from the same point simultaneously, they meet again at the starting point exactly at the LCM of the times taken by each to complete one full round independently.

Meeting First Time Anywhere on Track

If running in the same direction, Time to meet = Track Length ÷ (S₁ − S₂). If running in opposite directions, Time to meet = Track Length ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Number of Distinct Meeting Points

If the ratio of their speeds is a : b in its simplest form, they will meet at (a − b) distinct points if running in the same direction, and at (a + b) distinct points if running in opposite directions.
</p
